description: The Gujarat government has drafted a policy to provide artificial intelligence (AI) training to five lakh students across higher education institutions under the proposed Gujarat AI for Every Student Mission 2026–27. The initiative aims to introduce students to AI fundamentals, discipline-specific applications and advanced skills to improve their employability.Prepared by the state’s Higher Education Department, the draft policy proposes a three-tier training programme and the development of 5,000 faculty members as AI Master Trainers within 12 months. The state has proposed an allocation of ₹20 crore for the mission.However, the policy is yet to receive in-principle administrative and financial clearances. Its implementation will begin after the necessary approvals are secured.Three-Tier AI Training Programme ProposedThe proposed mission will offer training at three levels, allowing students to progress from basic AI literacy to specialised applications and advanced, project-based learning.The first level, AI Foundation for Every Student, will be an eight-hour introductory course targeting five lakh students. It will cover AI fundamentals, generative AI tools, prompting techniques, applications in learning and productivity, and responsible use of AI-generated information.The second level, AI for Domain Applications, will offer 25 hours of training to one lakh students. The course will focus on applying AI within eight broad academic streams, including commerce and management, engineering and technology, arts and humanities, science and mathematics, education, agriculture, healthcare, and law and public administration.The third level, Advanced AI Skills and Employability, will provide 50 hours of blended, project-based training to 20,000 students. The proposed curriculum includes advanced AI tools, specialised technical skills, industry case studies, practical assessments and capstone projects.Students will generally progress to the next level after completing the preceding course or demonstrating equivalent competency.Gujarat Plans To Train 5,000 Faculty MembersAlongside student training, the draft policy proposes developing a network of 5,000 faculty members as AI Master Trainers within 12 months. They are expected to support AI training across participating colleges and universities.The implementation framework will include a State Mission Unit to coordinate the programme. Universities will nominate nodal officers, while individual colleges will appoint coordinators to oversee training and monitor student participation.AI Courses To Be Offered In English And GujaratiThe proposed learning modules will be available in English and Gujarati to support wider participation across the state.The curriculum will also emphasise responsible AI use, data security and the verification of AI-generated outputs. Students will be encouraged to critically evaluate information produced by AI systems rather than accept it without scrutiny.A statewide dashboard is also proposed to track enrolment, certification and student progression across the three training levels. Unique learner IDs, institutional reviews and independent verification of selected outcomes are among the planned monitoring measures.₹20 Crore Allocation Awaits Government ApprovalThe proposed ₹20 crore allocation will support the mission, subject to the required administrative and financial clearances.Under the draft plan, the state aims to provide foundational AI training to five lakh students, offer domain-specific learning to one lakh students and deliver advanced training to 20,000 students.The final implementation schedule and operational details will depend on the approvals granted and arrangements made by the Higher Education Department and participating institutions.
